reference_action: Borderline mixed pest/sun-stress case: owner reports improvement after alcohol wiping, soap/alcohol washing, horticultural-oil wiping, insecticidal soap and systemic granules. Neem retreatment is planned; no single product is causally validated. Count comparable pest removal/oil/soap/systemic treatment, not inspection alone.

sources.reason: Neem-oil treatment is functionally comparable to the owner-applied horticultural oil; partial bundle match only, no proof neem alone worked.
Root/drainage and drought care; shower instruction is irrigation, not leaf pest removal.
Explicit systemic granules, showering and soap/alcohol pest treatment match multiple owner actions.
Describes and identifies BOP diseases, mites and mealybugs but gives no treatment.

actions.action: Keep soil damp with adequate drainage

resolved.reason: Possible bugs and oil treatment overlap the pest-removal bundle, but mixed watering/bruising explanations, vague neem instructions and incomplete Epsom advice do not constitute a clear main fix.

harmfulness.reason: “Add a bit of Epsom salt” lacks indication and dose; neem lacks sunlight/application precautions. Conflicting damp-soil and fixed-schedule advice also risks inappropriate watering, though drainage is explicitly required.

specificity_accuracy.reason: “White spots which may [be] bugs or a fungus” recognizes pests on the correct species. The discussion also assumes bruising or watering trouble and does not resolve the observed insects or acute light-change damage.

feasibility.reason: Oil, bottom watering and moving the pot are ordinary actions. Unspecified oil/salt amounts and incompatible watering directions leave important decisions to the novice.
